wu: Warm-up: 'Find Someone Who...' Students mingle, ask 'Is [city] more modern than [city]?', and write names. Teacher models 'Is Rabat more historic than Casablanca?', students reply 'Yes, it is' or 'No, it isn't'.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'City Comparison Pairs' - Teacher writes two cities on board, students shout out differences (bigger, older, noisier)
Alternative 2: 'Guess the City' - Teacher gives clues 'It's smaller than Casablanca but more famous for tourism', students guess
pres: Presentation: Show two phone flashcards (iPhone vs Samsung). Model 'The iPhone is more expensive than the Samsung'. Elicit 'more... than' for longer adjectives. Drill with 'Rabat is older than Agadir' and 'Casablanca is bigger than Fes'. Check with 'Which is bigger?' questions.
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use local band posters (L'mencha vs Hoba') to compare 'more popular' and 'better'
Alternative 2: Bring two food items (orange juice vs mint tea) to compare 'sweeter' and 'more refreshing'
prac: Guided practice: 'Comparative Race' - In pairs, students get a list of adjective pairs (big/small, old/new). They race to write 5 correct sentences. Teacher monitors for 'more' vs '-er' errors. Support with sentence frames '[A] is [comparative] than [B]'.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Find the Difference' - Students compare two pictures of Moroccan cities (old medina vs new city) using comparatives
Alternative 2: 'Adjective Swap' - Students write 3 adjectives, swap with partner, and make comparative sentences
ls: Listening slot: Play an audio of two tourists comparing Oujda and Tangier. Students tick 'True' or 'False' on a handout with statements like 'Oujda is more beautiful than Tangier'. Replay to check answers.
re: Reactivation game: 'Stand Up If...' Teacher says 'Stand up if your city is more modern than your partner's'. Students stand, say '[My city] is more modern', and sit down.
prod: Production task: 'Cafe Comparison Roleplay' - In groups of 3, students roleplay a conversation comparing two cafes (one local, one American). They use 'more expensive', 'better coffee', 'noisier', and 'friendlier'. Teacher circulates, noting good use of 'much/a lot/far'.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Students read a short text comparing Marrakech and Chefchaouen. Underline all comparatives with 'much' or 'a lot'. Then write 4 sentences about their own city using 'much bigger than' or 'a lot older than'.
st: Story/Song + Goodbye: Play 'The City Song' (comparative lyrics). Close with 'Today we learned to compare cities with comparatives. Thank you, class!'
g: Students write 9 comparatives on a grid. Teacher calls out sentences, students mark if true
Students get city cards, race to shout 3 comparatives when teacher shows two
Students race to write -er or more before adjectives on the board
Students find someone whose city is 'far older' than theirs and write it down
Students form a chain: 'Rabat is older than...' next student adds '...but smaller than...'
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences comparing Oujda and another Moroccan city using 'much/a lot/far'
Support: Use a word bank with comparatives (bigger, older, more expensive) to complete sentences
hw: Option 1: Write a paragraph comparing two Moroccan cities (6-8 sentences)
Option 2: Record a voice note comparing two phones or bands
Option 3: Draw two pictures and label 5 comparatives (e.g., 'taller', 'cheaper')
tip: Use local examples (Rabat vs Casablanca, mint tea vs coffee) to make comparisons meaningful and connect to learners' lives.
